Execute the Vietnam thermal generation inventory in phases. TURN 1 — COAL PLANTS DISCOVERY: Search for Vietnam's coal-fired power plants systematically. Cover: (a) currently operating coal plants, (b) plants under construction, (c) planned/announced coal plants per PDP8, (d) cancelled/shelved coal projects. For each, capture: Vietnamese name, English name, province, technology (subcritical/supercritical/USC), unit configuration, total MWe, status, COD, owner/developer. Use the evidence pack (PDP7, PDP7A, PDP8 annexes, EVN ARs) as the backbone and supplement with targeted web searches. Compile a working list with source annotations. TURN 2 — GAS & LNG PLANTS DISCOVERY: Search for Vietnam's gas-fired and LNG-to-power plants. Cover: (a) operating domestic-gas plants (Phú Mỹ complex, Cà Mau, Nhơn Trạch, etc.), (b) LNG-to-power projects (Nhơn Trạch 3&4, Bạc Liêu, Sơn Mỹ, Long An, Quảng Ninh, Hải Lăng, etc.), (c) cancelled/shelved gas projects. Capture same attributes. Cross-reference PDP8 Annex II tables for planned gas/LNG capacity. TURN 3 — REPORT COMPILATION: Produce the final Markdown inventory document. Begin directly with the single pipe table (all assets, all fuels, all statuses in one table). Follow with per-asset notes for major/disputed/ambiguous assets. End with annotated bibliography. Apply confidence rules strictly. Reconcile any conflicts found in Turns 1-2. Ensure arithmetic consistency (Units×MW = Total MWe or explain). Flag temporal freshness issues. TURN 4 — VERIFY & POLISH: Review the report for: (a) missing known assets, (b) arithmetic errors, (c) confidence miscalibration, (d) source gaps, (e) status/date consistency. ## Per-Asset Notes

**#1 Uông Bí (original), #6 Ninh Bình — Retirement.** PDP7A Annex I explicitly listed "NĐ Uông Bí ngừng phát điện 105 MW" under 2021 entries. Similarly, PDP7 Annex II listed Ninh Bình 100 MW for retirement in 2021. The original Uông Bí plant disappeared from EVN AR 2018 rosters. Both are assessed as Retired; confidence MEDIUM because no formal MOIT retirement notice was found via web search.

**#16 Thái Bình 2.** Severely delayed from original PDP7 target of 2014–15, then PDP7A target of 2017–18. Revised PDP8 sources indicate coal capacity of 31,055 MW, consistent with Thái Bình 2 being operational. Report 32 noted "Chưa xác định tiến độ hoàn thành" as of its writing. Multiple Vietnamese media sources confirm COD in 2022–23.

**#27 Vân Phong 1 (BOT).** Revised PDP8 implementation plan lists Quảng Trạch I with COD 2025 and Long Phú I with COD 2026, implying Vân Phong 1 is already completed. Confirmed via MOIT and Sumitomo announcements: COD January 24, 2024. At 2×716 MW = 1,432 MW, this is Vietnam's only USC coal plant.

**#37 Formosa Hà Tĩnh (Phase 1).** Complex captive/industrial plant with multiple unit types. PDP7A listed units #2 (150 MW coal, COD 2012), #3,4 (2×100 MW BFG, COD 2016), #5 (150 MW coal, COD 2016). Total ~500 MW. Not a standard grid plant; included because individual units exceed 30 MWe threshold.

**#42 Long Phú I — Stalled construction.** Study E-542 reported "hoàn thành 78% tiến độ nhưng tạm ngừng" (78% complete but suspended) due to US sanctions on Russian contractor Power Machines. Report 58 noted delays of potentially 48+ months. Revised PDP8 now targets Long Phú I COD in 2026, though this remains uncertain. Confidence LOW.

**#43–46 Shelved coal BOT projects.** PDP8 Annex II Table 3 listed these as "chậm tiến độ, gặp khó khăn" (delayed, facing difficulties). The June 2024 deadline applied specifically to Công Thanh (#47); it was subsequently converted to LNG under Revised PDP8. The other four remain formally in PDP8 but with no investor progress. All four BOT developers face financing difficulties in the post-Paris Agreement coal-exit environment.

**#48 Hải Hà 1 (cogeneration).** PDP8 Table 4 lists 300 MW. PDP7A targeted COD 2019 for Phase 1 (3×50 MW). Located within Texhong industrial zone, Quảng Ninh. Status and actual capacity difficult to verify; confidence LOW.

**#64–65 Nhơn Trạch 3 & 4.** On December 14, 2025, the inauguration ceremony was held at Ong Keo Industrial Park, Dong Nai Province. Total designed capacity of 1,624 MW; each unit ~812 MW. Uses GE's 9HA.02 gas turbines with efficiency of 62–64%. Total investment of about USD 1.4 billion. This is Vietnam's first power complex to use imported LNG as fuel. LNG sourced from Thị Vải LNG Terminal (~24 km away). PPA and gas supply agreement challenges noted but resolved by inauguration.

**#63 Ô Môn I.** Currently operates on oil (660 MW per evn_ar_2017/2018). PDP8 Table 5 lists it for conversion to Block B domestic gas. Fuel switch contingent on Block B pipeline completion (est. end 2026).

**#66 Ô Môn III.** PM agreed to change investor from EVN to Petrovietnam in June 2023. In March 2025, a ceremony formalised the connection agreement for O Mon III CCGT to the National Power System. Construction scheduled to start Q1 2025, with gas receipt Q3 2027 and grid connection Q4 2027. Capacity 1,050 MW.

**#67 Ô Môn IV.** Ground-breaking took place in late August 2025, with operational target December 2028. Doosan Enerbility signed EPC contract worth ~US$770 million in June 2025. Mitsubishi Power contracted to supply two M701JAC gas turbines. ADB loan of US$309.89 million approved.

**#68 Ô Môn II.** Proposed 1,050 MW. Vietracimex-Marubeni JV approved by PM in 2019, with output increased from 750 MW to 1,050 MW. Still in investment preparation; no construction started. Revised PDP8 groups O Mon I–IV at collective 3,810 MW with COD between 2025 and 2030.

**Block B – Ô Môn gas supply chain.** Block B production scheduled to start by end of 2026, with estimated capacity of 490 million cubic feet per day. 431 km pipeline will supply O Mon I, II, III, and IV with total capacity of ~3,180 MW. FID taken in early 2024.

**#69–73 Dung Quất I–III and Miền Trung I–II.** All dependent on Cá Voi Xanh (Blue Whale) gas field development by ExxonMobil. Dung Quất I-III have collective capacity of 2,250 MW and expected COD in 2030. Blue Whale development has faced repeated delays; FID not yet taken as of mid-2025. All assessed Pre-permit/LOW confidence.

**#88 LNG Bạc Liêu.** 3,200 MW power plant with estimated cost of US$4 billion. Invested by American firm Delta Offshore Energy, granted investment certificate in 2020, but has yet to commence construction. Listed in Revised PDP8 (April 2025) for 2025–2030 period. EVNNPT and Bac Lieu LNG Power signed grid connection agreement in March 2026 for connection via 500 kV Bạc Liêu–Thốt Nốt line. Despite progress on approvals, no PPA finalized and no construction start confirmed. Assessed Permitted/MEDIUM.

**Revised PDP8 (Decision 768/QĐ-TTg, April 15, 2025).** Total coal capacity set at 31,055 MW, fully implemented by 2030. Coal plants shall only commence operation until 2030; beyond 2030, plants must shift to biomass/ammonia or shut down after 40 years. O Mon I–IV collective capacity 3,810 MW, COD 2025–2030; Dung Quất I–III 2,250 MW, COD 2030.

**Cancelled coal projects not listed in table.** Numerous PDP7/PDP7A coal projects were not carried into PDP8 and are considered Cancelled: Cẩm Phả III (440 MW), Hải Phòng III (1,200+ MW), Quảng Ninh III (1,200 MW), Quỳnh Lập I & II coal (2,400 MW total — now considered for LNG), Long Phú II (1,320 MW), Long Phú III (1,800 MW), Kiên Lương I/II/III (3,600+ MW — license revoked), Tân Phước I & II (2,400 MW), Vũng Áng III coal (1,200–2,400 MW), Bạc Liêu I coal (1,200 MW contingency), and several far-future generic entries from PDP7 Annex II (Bình Định, An Giang, Sông Hậu III etc.).

## Per-Asset Notes

**#1 Uông Bí (original), #6 Ninh Bình — Retirement.** PDP7A Annex I explicitly listed "NĐ Uông Bí ngừng phát điện 105 MW" under 2021 entries. Similarly, PDP7 Annex II listed Ninh Bình 100 MW for retirement in 2021. The original Uông Bí plant disappeared from EVN AR 2018 rosters. Both are assessed as Retired; confidence MEDIUM because no formal MOIT retirement notice was found via web search.

**#16 Thái Bình 2.** Severely delayed from original PDP7 target of 2014–15, then PDP7A target of 2017–18. Revised PDP8 sources indicate coal capacity of 31,055 MW, consistent with Thái Bình 2 being operational. Report 32 noted "Chưa xác định tiến độ hoàn thành" as of its writing. Multiple Vietnamese media sources confirm COD in 2022–23.

**#27 Vân Phong 1 (BOT).** Revised PDP8 implementation plan lists Quảng Trạch I with COD 2025 and Long Phú I with COD 2026, implying Vân Phong 1 is already completed. Confirmed via MOIT and Sumitomo announcements: COD January 24, 2024. At 2×716 MW = 1,432 MW, this is Vietnam's only USC coal plant.

**#37 Formosa Hà Tĩnh (Phase 1).** Complex captive/industrial plant with multiple unit types. PDP7A listed units #2 (150 MW coal, COD 2012), #3,4 (2×100 MW BFG, COD 2016), #5 (150 MW coal, COD 2016). Total ~500 MW. Not a standard grid plant; included because individual units exceed 30 MWe threshold.

**#42 Long Phú I — Stalled construction.** Study E-542 reported "hoàn thành 78% tiến độ nhưng tạm ngừng" (78% complete but suspended) due to US sanctions on Russian contractor Power Machines. Report 58 noted delays of potentially 48+ months. Revised PDP8 now targets Long Phú I COD in 2026, though this remains uncertain. Confidence LOW.

**#43–46 Shelved coal BOT projects.** PDP8 Annex II Table 3 listed these as "chậm tiến độ, gặp khó khăn" (delayed, facing difficulties). The June 2024 deadline applied specifically to Công Thanh (#47); it was subsequently converted to LNG under Revised PDP8. The other four remain formally in PDP8 but with no investor progress. All four BOT developers face financing difficulties in the post-Paris Agreement coal-exit environment.

**#48 Hải Hà 1 (cogeneration).** PDP8 Table 4 lists 300 MW. PDP7A targeted COD 2019 for Phase 1 (3×50 MW). Located within Texhong industrial zone, Quảng Ninh. Status and actual capacity difficult to verify; confidence LOW.

**#64–65 Nhơn Trạch 3 & 4.** On December 14, 2025, the inauguration ceremony was held at Ong Keo Industrial Park, Dong Nai Province. Total designed capacity of 1,624 MW; each unit ~812 MW. Uses GE's 9HA.02 gas turbines with efficiency of 62–64%. Total investment of about USD 1.4 billion. This is Vietnam's first power complex to use imported LNG as fuel. LNG sourced from Thị Vải LNG Terminal (~24 km away). PPA and gas supply agreement challenges noted but resolved by inauguration.

**#63 Ô Môn I.** Currently operates on oil (660 MW per evn_ar_2017/2018). PDP8 Table 5 lists it for conversion to Block B domestic gas. Fuel switch contingent on Block B pipeline completion (est. end 2026).

**#66 Ô Môn III.** PM agreed to change investor from EVN to Petrovietnam in June 2023. In March 2025, a ceremony formalised the connection agreement for O Mon III CCGT to the National Power System. Construction scheduled to start Q1 2025, with gas receipt Q3 2027 and grid connection Q4 2027. Capacity 1,050 MW.

**#67 Ô Môn IV.** Ground-breaking took place in late August 2025, with operational target December 2028. Doosan Enerbility signed EPC contract worth ~US$770 million in June 2025. Mitsubishi Power contracted to supply two M701JAC gas turbines. ADB loan of US$309.89 million approved.

**#68 Ô Môn II.** Proposed 1,050 MW. Vietracimex-Marubeni JV approved by PM in 2019, with output increased from 750 MW to 1,050 MW. Still in investment preparation; no construction started. Revised PDP8 groups O Mon I–IV at collective 3,810 MW with COD between 2025 and 2030.

**Block B – Ô Môn gas supply chain.** Block B production scheduled to start by end of 2026, with estimated capacity of 490 million cubic feet per day. 431 km pipeline will supply O Mon I, II, III, and IV with total capacity of ~3,180 MW. FID taken in early 2024.

**#69–73 Dung Quất I–III and Miền Trung I–II.** All dependent on Cá Voi Xanh (Blue Whale) gas field development by ExxonMobil. Dung Quất I-III have collective capacity of 2,250 MW and expected COD in 2030. Blue Whale development has faced repeated delays; FID not yet taken as of mid-2025. All assessed Pre-permit/LOW confidence.

**#88 LNG Bạc Liêu.** 3,200 MW power plant with estimated cost of US$4 billion. Invested by American firm Delta Offshore Energy, granted investment certificate in 2020, but has yet to commence construction. Listed in Revised PDP8 (April 2025) for 2025–2030 period. EVNNPT and Bac Lieu LNG Power signed grid connection agreement in March 2026 for connection via 500 kV Bạc Liêu–Thốt Nốt line. Despite progress on approvals, no PPA finalized and no construction start confirmed. Assessed Permitted/MEDIUM.

**Revised PDP8 (Decision 768/QĐ-TTg, April 15, 2025).** Total coal capacity set at 31,055 MW, fully implemented by 2030. Coal plants shall only commence operation until 2030; beyond 2030, plants must shift to biomass/ammonia or shut down after 40 years. O Mon I–IV collective capacity 3,810 MW, COD 2025–2030; Dung Quất I–III 2,250 MW, COD 2030.

**Cancelled coal projects not listed in table.** Numerous PDP7/PDP7A coal projects were not carried into PDP8 and are considered Cancelled: Cẩm Phả III (440 MW), Hải Phòng III (1,200+ MW), Quảng Ninh III (1,200 MW), Quỳnh Lập I & II coal (2,400 MW total — now considered for LNG), Long Phú II (1,320 MW), Long Phú III (1,800 MW), Kiên Lương I/II/III (3,600+ MW — license revoked), Tân Phước I & II (2,400 MW), Vũng Áng III coal (1,200–2,400 MW), Bạc Liêu I coal (1,200 MW contingency), and several far-future generic entries from PDP7 Annex II (Bình Định, An Giang, Sông Hậu III etc.).
